findings.evidence: Lines 91–92 define the body directly, and line 104 itself exposes it with `rw [extendedRelNormHom, ...]`; the same unfolding is available to importing consumers.
findings.fix: Replace this rationale with the accurate, narrower point that no dedicated computation lemma would be available under only `IsDomain A`.
findings.issue: The implementation note says a weaker definition would have an “unexposed body” and be “opaque to every consumer,” but consumers can explicitly unfold a `def` and expose `relNorm.comp (extendedHom A M)` across module boundaries.

findings.evidence: The declaration at lines 81–85 has independent parameters `A M R` but no inequality constraint, so the interface itself does not make them distinct.
findings.fix: State only that separate type parameters support the intended cross-ring use, and describe any same-ring elaboration limitation without claiming enforced distinctness.
findings.issue: The note claims the three types are distinct and avoid the same-ring instance diamond “by construction,” but Lean type variables are not constrained to be unequal; callers may instantiate `A` and `R` with the same type.

summary: The module documentation makes two inaccurate claims about unfolding definitions and type parameters.
